title: The Sorry Garden
rule: Every time you say sorry, a flower grows on your head.
ending: The whole town becomes a field of flowers on heads, and the Mayor's top hat lifts off on a giant sunflower stem after he says sorry last.

planted.detail: A tiny red flower on my head after my first sorry
Mayor's tall top hat on his bare head

lines.text: In this town, every sorry grows a flower on your head.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Everyone walks carefully across the cobbled square.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Yesterday I bumped into my little sister in the kitchen.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: I said sorry, and a tiny red flower popped up.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Mom smiled and watered it with a cup.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: At school, I stepped on a classmate's backpack.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: I said sorry again, and a yellow flower grew.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: The teacher had a whole bouquet on her head.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Then the Mayor marched out in front of the town hall.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: His tall top hat sat proudly on his bare head.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Then a blue bird landed and knocked his hat off.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Everyone gasped. A crowd of flower heads leaned in.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: My little red flower waved, as if it knew.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: He mumbled sorry, and a giant sunflower shot up.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: His top hat rose high, held up on the stem.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: Now the whole town is a garden of heads.
lines.speaker: narrator

lines.text: In this town, who will be brave enough to say sorry first?
lines.speaker: narrator
